Subject: NimbusAI post-demo: private deployment data & PII follow-ups

Hi Sofia / Alex —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciated the honest signal on latency targets and the constraint that all model inputs from your production inference flows are treated as regulated PII. Per our conversation, I wanted to summarize the immediate qualification asks and propose next steps so we can align engineering scopes for a private/VPC pilot.

Quick recap of what we heard:
- Scope: user-submitted prompts and user metadata (email, org id) are considered PII and must not leave NimbusAI-controlled storage.
- Requirement: private deployment (VPC with no public egress) preferred; on-prem or air-gapped evaluation possible for regulatory pilots.
- Retention: default logs/telemetry must be configurable; Nimbus wants 30–90 day retention, optional archival to customer-managed S3 with CMEK.
- Audit: need request/response audit logs and access logs for model invocations; Redaction option desired for saved prompts.
- Egress: strict rule — no model payloads or KV cache uploaded to third-party services; outbound telemetry limited to ops metrics only and routable to customer endpoint.

Immediate asks from your team (as I captured):
1) Please send your security questionnaire (we can map answers to SOC2 controls).
2) Confirm whether the pilot can allow a dedicated VPC with a controlled NAT (we discussed a block rule set to prevent internet egress).
3) Share a simple dataflow diagram showing where PII originates and any downstream systems that currently store logs/outputs.

What we'll deliver next:
- Marcus will put together a short private-deploy dataflow diagram and a matrix of controls (retention, encryption, logging toggles, egress gating).
- I'll prepare a one-page mutual action plan (timeline, milestones, ownership).

Attachments: I can share our private deployment architecture sketch and MAP after Marcus adds the infra specifics.

Next step: can we schedule an hour on Tue/Wed to walk the questionnaire and the control matrix? I put a tentative window in the HubSpot record.

Thanks —
Karthik

- PII scope: includes free-text prompts and any system-generated transcripts we store. For pilot we can scope to a single customer segment where PII risk surface is smaller.
- Retention target: compliance wants default 30 days for searchable logs, 90 days archival is OK if archival is encrypted with our KMS.

3) If we choose customer-managed S3 for archival, can you support customer KMS keys?

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for the questionnaire — I started mapping answers inline and wanted to call out concrete controls that address your numbered questions:

1) Model input logging: yes, per-deployment toggle. In Redwood Private a deployment config exposes three logging modes: OFF (no request/response body persisted), METRICS_ONLY (latency/throughput counters + error codes), and FULL (bodies persisted to customer-controlled S3). For regulated pilots we recommend OFF or METRICS_ONLY, and we can enable redaction hooks before any persistence.

2) KV cache persistence: by default KV cache is kept in-memory and persisted to an ephemeral disk on the node for fast restarts; persistence is local to the VPC and encrypted at rest with the node's disk key. For stricter requirements we support an ephemeral-only mode (no disk write) — cache will repopulate on warmup and cold-start costs will be higher. We'll document expected latency impact for ephemeral-only mode.

3) Customer-managed S3 + KMS: supported. We support customer-managed buckets and CMEK (customer KMS) for archival of audit logs and model outputs. Access is restricted via the deployment VPC role and bucket policies we provide.

Other notes:
- Egress controls: you can deploy with a deny-all egress policy at the subnet/NAT level; our agent processes can be configured to route telemetry to a customer endpoint inside your VPC only. No outbound model payloads to Redwood-hosted services when that mode is selected.
- Audit logs & retention: we can ship two classes of logs — access/audit logs (who called what, with timestamps) and optional payload logs. Retention windows are configurable per-deployment; we support 30/90/365 day presets and custom values.
- Air-gapped: Redwood can run in a fully air-gapped on-prem mode. Control plane updates require a signed bundle that your ops team can pull and validate. There is an operational tradeoff (manual update cadence) we should document for your security team.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll attach a simple architecture PNG showing the private deployment flow (redwood_private_deploy_arch.png) with the egress gating options flagged.
- Karthik / I will fill the questionnaire rows and return an annotated copy.
- If Nimbus wants ephemeral-only KV and OFF logging, we should prototype a single-node pilot to measure cold-start impact.

Let me know which combination of logging + KV persistence you want us to annotate first — I can turn around the annotated questionnaire by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marcus
